methods.name: ParseElectricityRef
methods.doc:
Parses a Pakistani electricity bill identifier: a DISCO reference number,
a DISCO customer ID or a K-Electric account number.

Formats are those the utilities' own bill pages ask for (retrieved
2026-11-18; see DATA.md): PITC's bill pages take a 14-digit reference
number with a separate U/R choice, or a 10-digit customer ID (11 digits
for LESCO); K-Electric asks for a 13-digit account number starting
`04000`. No check digit is published, so only the format is checked.
Spaces, dashes and dots are ignored, and Urdu digits are accepted.

```csharp
Bills.ParseElectricityRef("02-12624-0045901 R");
// Type = Reference, Digits = 02126240045901, Formatted = 02 12624 0045901 R, UrbanRural = R, Disco = null
```

returns.doc: The identifier, or `null` if it matches none of the formats. Never throws.

methods.name: FindAll
methods.doc:
Finds CNIC numbers in free text, such as a chat message, a note or an
uploaded document, for example to mask them before logging.

Digits are read in groups (unbroken runs of digits). Groups may be
joined by any run of spaces or tabs, or by one mark (a hyphen or
Unicode dash, a dot, a slash or an underscore) with any spaces around
it: `35202 1234567 1`, `35202  1234567  1`,
`35202 -1234567- 1`, `35202_1234567_1`,
`35202 - 1234567 - 1`, `352 0212 3456 71`,
`35202/1234567/1`. A line break never joins groups. A match is
consecutive whole groups that add up to exactly 13 digits, starting
with a province code (1-8); the search goes on after each match, so
`0300-1234567 35202-1234567-1` finds the CNIC. A group is never
split, so 13 digits inside a longer unbroken number (an IBAN, a card
number) never match. Digits may be ASCII, Urdu or Arabic-Indic, even
mixed. This matches everything Jaanch's own CNIC redaction does, except
across line breaks.

Accepting any grouping catches CNICs as people really type them, but
matches more that is not a CNIC: any 13 digits starting with 1-8 split
into groups this way (an account, order or tracking number, table
columns, a price list such as `8260 - 8048 - 2804 - 0`, a file
name such as `IMG_20261123_12345`, or two shorter numbers written
together) are found. {@link Cnic.Validate} stays strict.

```csharp
Cnic.FindAll("CNIC: 35202-1234567-1, phone 0300-1234567");
// [CnicMatch { Raw = "35202-1234567-1", Digits = "3520212345671",
//   Formatted = "35202-1234567-1", Start = 6, End = 21 }]
Cnic.FindAll("id 352 0212 3456 71")[0].Digits;  // "3520212345671"
```

returns.doc: The matches in order, or an empty list (also for `null`). Never throws.

methods.name: FindAll
methods.signature: public static IReadOnlyList<CnicMatch> FindAll(string? text, bool acrossLines)
methods.doc:
Finds CNIC numbers in free text, as {@link Cnic.FindAll}
does, optionally also joining digit groups across a single line break.

With `acrossLines`, a single line break (`\r\n`,
`\r` or `\n`, with any spaces around it) also joins groups,
like a space, so a CNIC written over several lines is found; a blank
line (two or more line breaks) never joins them. This can also join
numbers on consecutive lines, such as a list of amounts.

```csharp
Cnic.FindAll("CNIC\n35202\n1234567\n1", acrossLines: true)[0].Formatted;  // "35202-1234567-1"
```

params.name: acrossLines
params.doc: Also join digit groups across single line breaks.

returns.doc: The matches in order, or an empty list (also for `null`). Never throws.

methods.name: Mask
methods.signature:
public static MaskedText Mask(
    string? text,
    string? mask = "X",
    string? replacement = null)
methods.doc:
Masks every CNIC in free text, as found by {@link Cnic.FindAll}: each
digit becomes `mask` and the separators stay, so
`35202-1234567-1` becomes `XXXXX-XXXXXXX-X`. The rest of the
text is unchanged. With `replacement`, each whole CNIC
is replaced by that text instead.

Like {@link Cnic.FindAll}, it also masks any other 13 digits that start
with 1-8, however they are grouped.

```csharp
Cnic.Mask("My CNIC is 35202-1234567-1");  // Text = "My CNIC is XXXXX-XXXXXXX-X", Count = 1
Cnic.Mask("35202 1234567 1", "*");        // Text = "***** ******* *", Count = 1
Cnic.Mask("CNIC 352 0212 3456 71", replacement: "[CNIC removed]");
// Text = "CNIC [CNIC removed]", Count = 1
```

params.name: mask
params.doc: The string that replaces each digit. `null` means `"X"`.

params.name: replacement
params.doc: The string that replaces each whole CNIC, separators included, e.g. `"[CNIC removed]"`. Takes precedence over `mask`; `null` means no replacement.

returns.doc: The masked text (or replaced, with `replacement`) and the number of CNICs masked; `("", 0)` for `null` text. Never throws.

methods.name: Mask
methods.signature:
public static MaskedText Mask(
    string? text,
    bool acrossLines,
    string? mask = "X",
    string? replacement = null)
methods.doc:
Masks every CNIC in free text, as
{@link Cnic.Mask} does, optionally also
finding CNICs written across single line breaks, as
{@link Cnic.FindAll} does.

With `mask` the line breaks inside a CNIC stay; with
`replacement` they are replaced with the rest of the CNIC.

```csharp
Cnic.Mask("35202\n1234567\n1", acrossLines: true);  // Text = "XXXXX\nXXXXXXX\nX", Count = 1
Cnic.Mask("35202\n1234567\n1", acrossLines: true, replacement: "[CNIC removed]");
// Text = "[CNIC removed]", Count = 1
```

params.name: acrossLines
params.doc: Also join digit groups across single line breaks.

params.name: mask
params.doc: The string that replaces each digit. `null` means `"X"`.

params.name: replacement
params.doc: The string that replaces each whole CNIC, separators included. Takes precedence over `mask`; `null` means no replacement.

returns.doc: The masked text and the number of CNICs masked; `("", 0)` for `null` text. Never throws.

entries.name: Courier
entries.doc:
Helpers for orders shipped with Pakistani couriers (TCS, Leopards, PostEx,
M&P, Trax, BlueEx). There are no API clients: nothing is sent anywhere.

methods.name: MapStatus
methods.signature: public static CourierStatus? MapStatus(string? courier, string? raw)
methods.doc:
Maps a courier's own status name or code, as the courier documents it,
to a {@link CourierStatus}. Matching ignores case and extra
spaces; PostEx's "Attempt Made: <reason>" history messages map to
{@link CourierStatus.Attempted}.

Only statuses the courier documents publicly are mapped: PostEx's API
guide and one Leopards status. TCS, M&P, Trax and BlueEx publish no
list, so they always return `null`, as does any status not in the
list. No API is called.

Experimental: only PostEx and one Leopards status are mapped so far. The
mapping and the {@link CourierStatus} values may change in a minor
release as other couriers' lists are added.

params.name: raw
params.doc: The status as the courier returned it.

returns.doc: The status, or `null`. Never throws.

methods.name: MapStatus
methods.signature: public static CourierStatus? MapStatus(string? courier, double raw)
methods.doc:
Maps a courier's numeric status ID (e.g. PostEx's `5`) to a
{@link CourierStatus}. The number must be a non-negative whole
number (`5` and `5.0` are the same; `1.5`, `-1` and
NaN return `null`); it is looked up as its decimal string, so
`5` matches `"5"` but not `"0005"`.

Experimental, like {@link Courier.MapStatus}.

params.name: raw
params.doc: The status ID as the courier returned it.

returns.doc: The status, or `null`. Never throws.

methods.name: NormalizeCity
methods.doc:
Maps the way a customer or a courier writes a city to the city's name in
the city list, so orders can be matched against a courier's service
list. Accepts the exact name in any case, short forms (`LHR`,
`Khi`, `Pindi`, `Isb`, `FSD`), the old name
Lyallpur, a trailing "city", and the main cities in Urdu script.

```csharp
Courier.NormalizeCity("LHR");          // "Lahore"
Courier.NormalizeCity("lyallpur");     // "Faisalabad"
Courier.NormalizeCity("Karachi City"); // "Karachi"
Courier.NormalizeCity("Atlantis");     // null
```

returns.doc: A city from the city list, or `null`. Never throws.

entries.name: FbrInvoice
entries.doc:
FBR Digital Invoicing (DI): a builder that works out the sales tax on the
invoice JSON posted to PRAL's gateway, and an offline validator for the
rules that can be checked without FBR's reference APIs.

Built from PRAL's "Technical Specification for DI API", version 1.12, and
PRAL's "Error Message Guide (Sales)"; see DATA.md. Nothing here talks to
FBR: there is no HTTP client and no token handling. Values that only FBR's
reference APIs can confirm (provinces, HS codes, units, rates, sale types,
SRO numbers) are checked for presence, not against FBR's lists, unless the
app passes the lists it synced from those APIs ({@link FbrInvoiceReference}).

The invoice is JSON ({@link JsonNode}), with the specification's
camelCase keys, because that is what is posted to FBR and what arrives
from untrusted sources. A JSON number is a number however it is written
(`5` or `5.0`); a number in a string (`"5"`) is not.

fields.name: SpecVersion
fields.doc: Version of PRAL's technical specification this module follows (`FBR_DI_SPEC_VERSION`).

methods.name: GetSaleTypes

returns.doc: The sale types, in the specification's order.

methods.name: ExpectedSalesTax
methods.doc:
The sales tax FBR expects on a line, in rupees, or `null` when the
rate is not a plain percentage or per-unit amount (spec §7, errors
0102, 0104, 0105).

`N%` on Third Schedule goods: retail price × rate (0102);
`N%` otherwise: value excluding sales tax × rate (0104);
`Rs.N`: quantity × N (0105). Rounded half up to the paisa.

```csharp
FbrInvoice.ExpectedSalesTax(JsonNode.Parse("""{"rate":"18%","valueSalesExcludingST":1000}""")); // 180
```

params.name: item
params.doc: One line of an invoice (a JSON object).

returns.doc: The tax, or `null`. Never throws.

methods.name: Build
methods.doc:
Builds an FBR digital invoice from your own fields, working out
`salesTaxApplicable` on each line where you leave it out (see
{@link FbrInvoice.ExpectedSalesTax}; uses {@link SalesTax.Calculate}).

Lines with a rate that is neither `N%` nor `Rs.N`
(`Exempt`, combined rates) get 0 unless you give the tax.
`salesTaxWithheldAtSource`, `totalValues` and
`fixedNotifiedValueOrRetailPrice` default to 0, and
`invoiceRefNo` and `buyerNTNCNIC` to `""`, as in FBR's
samples. Nothing else is filled in or changed (other keys are kept);
check the result with {@link FbrInvoice.Validate}. The
input is not modified: the invoice is a new copy.

params.name: input
params.doc: The invoice JSON, with an `items` array of objects.

returns.doc: The invoice and column totals, or `null` if `input` is not an object with an `items` array of objects. Never throws.

methods.name: Validate
methods.signature: public static FbrInvoiceValidation Validate(JsonNode? invoice, string? today = null)
methods.doc:
Checks an FBR digital invoice against the rules of PRAL's specification
(v1.12) and Error Message Guide that need no call to FBR, and returns
every problem with FBR's error code.

Checked: invoice type (0003, 0011), date format (0005, 0042, 0113) and,
with `today`, a future date (0043); seller and buyer
NTN/CNIC (0401, 0402, 0009), self-invoicing (0058), names, provinces
(0073, 0074), addresses, buyer registration type (0012), the reference
number of a debit note (0026), the sandbox scenario, and on each line:
HS code (0044), rate (0020), unit, sale type (0013), required and valid
amounts (0021, 0023, 0024, 0098, 0300, 0302), SRO schedule and serial
(0077, 0078), Third Schedule retail price (0090), extra tax on
reduced-rate goods (0091) and the sales tax arithmetic (0102, 0104,
0105, to within one paisa).

Not checked, because they need FBR's data: registration status, whether
a province, HS code, unit, rate, sale type or SRO is in FBR's lists or
fits the others, and the original invoice of a debit note.

params.name: invoice

methods.name: FormatLakh
methods.doc:
Formats an amount with lakh/crore units (`25 Lakh`, `1 Crore`).
Values are rounded to two decimals before the unit is chosen, so
`9999999` gives `1 Crore`. Smaller amounts fall back to
{@link Currency.FormatPkr}.

returns.doc: The formatted amount.

methods.name: ParseAmount
methods.doc:
Reads a rupee amount the way people type it in Pakistan, and returns it in
rupees, rounded half-up to the paisa. Returns `null` for anything that is
not exactly one non-negative amount; it never throws.

Accepted:

- digits, with or without grouping: `150000`, `150,000` (international) or `1,50,000` (Pakistani: groups of two, then three), and decimals (`1,234.50`, `.5`, `5.`); a grouping must be complete and consistent;
- Urdu (`۱۵۰۰۰۰`) and Arabic-Indic (`١٥٠٠٠٠`) digits, also mixed with 0-9, and the Arabic decimal and thousands separators (`٫`, `٬`);
- one currency mark before or after the number: `Rs`, `Rs.`, `PKR` or `₨` (any case), and a trailing `/-` (`Rs. 5,000/-`);
- one shorthand unit after the number, with or without a space, in any case: `k`, `thousand(s)`, `hazar`, `ہزار` (× 1,000); `lakh(s)`, `lac(s)`, `لاکھ` (× 100,000); `crore(s)`, `cr`, `کروڑ` (× 10,000,000). Decimals work with units: `1.5 lakh` is 150,000 and `2.25cr` is 22,500,000;
- whitespace around and between the parts (spaces, tabs, line breaks and no-break spaces).

Rejected (`null`): empty input, negative or signed amounts (`-500`,
`+500`), ranges (`5-10k`), more than one number (`500 600`), two currency
marks or two units, leftover letters (`500 rupees`, `5kk`), grouping that
could be read two ways or is broken (`1,50`, `1.500,00`, `1,5000`), and
amounts over Rs. 50 trillion (50 lakh crore), beyond which a number can no
longer hold every paisa exactly.

The arithmetic is done on the digits, so the result is exact: `1.005`
rounds to 1.01 and `1.5 lakh` is exactly 150000.

```csharp
Currency.ParseAmount("Rs. 1,50,000/-"); // ParsedAmount(150000, "Rs. 1,50,000/-")
Currency.ParseAmount("2.25cr");         // ParsedAmount(22500000, "2.25cr")
Currency.ParseAmount("5-10k");          // null
```

returns.doc: The value and raw input, or `null` if the input is not one amount.

methods.name: FormatAmountInput
methods.doc:
Writes back an amount typed in any form {@link Currency.ParseAmount} accepts, for
showing next to the field ("= Rs. 150,000"): `Rs.`, international
grouping, and paisa only when there are any (`Rs. 1,234.50`). Returns
`null` when {@link Currency.ParseAmount} does; it never throws.

returns.doc: E.g. `Rs. 150,000` for `1.5 lakh`, or `null`.

methods.name: ScoreAddress
methods.doc:
Scores how complete a free-form Pakistani delivery address is, for cash
on delivery and other courier use.

Built on {@link Address.Parse}. It looks for a city, a house, plot
or flat number, a street, an area, a postal code and a landmark
("near", "opp", "nazd", "qareeb", "سامنے" …), and adds up
{@link Quality.AddressWeights}. A postal code that is a known post office
raises the score more than an unknown one, and a post office in a
different province from the city lowers it (with a warning in
{@link ParsedAddress.Warnings}). This is a heuristic: it says how
much an address tells a rider, not whether the address exists.

```csharp
Quality.ScoreAddress("House 12, Street 4, Block B, Gulberg III, near Liberty Market, Lahore 54660");
// AddressScore { Score = 100, Missing = [], Parsed = … }
```

returns.doc: The score, the missing parts and the parsed address.

methods.name: PhoneRiskSignals
methods.doc:

looks made up. Pure heuristics on the number itself: no list of real
numbers, no personal data, no network call.

```csharp
Quality.PhoneRiskSignals("0301-2945716");  // []
Quality.PhoneRiskSignals("03001234567");   // [SequentialDigits, TestNumber]
Quality.PhoneRiskSignals("042 35761234");  // [Landline]
```

returns.doc: The flags; empty for a valid mobile number with nothing suspicious.

methods.name: Validate
methods.signature:
public static RaastQrValidation Validate(
    string? payload,
    DateTime? now = null,
    double expiresSoonMs = 3600000)
methods.doc:
Checks whether a Raast QR code can be paid. Errors: not a Pakistani
payment QR, checksum mismatch, a person-to-person QR with no IBAN, an
IBAN that fails its checksum, expired, or a fixed-amount QR without an
expiry. Warnings: an amount in a static QR (apps ignore it), a QR that
expires soon, or a merchant QR with no IBAN
({@link RaastQrWarning.NoIban}): merchant QRs may pay through the
merchant's own scheme, so it is valid, but the payee can't be checked
from the QR.

```csharp
RaastQr.Validate(scannedText);
// Valid = false, Kind = P2p, Errors = [Expired], Warnings = [], Qr = { ... }
```

params.name: payload
params.doc: Text decoded from the QR code.

params.name: now
params.doc: The time to check the expiry against. Defaults to the current local time.

params.name: expiresSoonMs
params.doc: How close to expiry counts as "soon", in milliseconds. Defaults to one hour.

returns.doc: Whether the QR is valid, with its errors, warnings and parsed form.

methods.name: RomanUrduKey
methods.doc:
A phonetic key for Roman Urdu, so that different spellings of the same
name or word match: `Mubeen` and `Mobeen`, `Muhammad`,
`Mohammad` and `Muhammed`, `Rehman` and `Rahman`,
`Chaudhry`, `Chaudhary` and `Chaudhery`. Compare keys,
not the text.

Each word keeps its consonants, its first vowel sound and a vowel sound
at its end. Letters for one sound are merged (`kh`, `sh`,
`ch`; `ph` and `f`; `q`, `c` and `k`;
`v` and `w`; `th` and `t`, `dh` and `d`),
doubled letters count once, `e` counts as `a`, `o` as
`u`, and a final `h` after a vowel is dropped. Accents are
removed and anything other than Latin letters splits words. The key is
not meant to be shown: it is an opaque string.

Different names can share a key (`Hamid` and `Hamad`), so
treat a match as "probably the same", not proof.
{@link Text.NormalizeRomanUrdu} is a different tool: it rewrites
informal spellings into readable text.

```csharp
Text.RomanUrduKey("Mubeen") == Text.RomanUrduKey("Mobeen");   // true
Text.RomanUrduKey("Muhammad Rehman");                          // "muhmd rahmn"
Text.RomanUrduKey("Hussain") == Text.RomanUrduKey("Hassan");   // false
```

returns.doc: The key, one part per word separated by spaces; `""` for text with no Latin letters or `null`. Never throws.

methods.name: Slugify
methods.signature: public static string Slugify(string? input, SlugifyOptions? options = null)
methods.doc:
Turns text into a URL slug: lower-case words joined by `-`.

Urdu letters are kept as they are (no transliteration: Urdu does not
write short vowels, so there is no single Roman spelling). Diacritics,
tatweel and zero-width characters are dropped, the Arabic look-alikes
ك ي ى become the Urdu ک ی ی, Urdu and Arabic-Indic digits become
`0-9`, and accented Latin-1 letters lose their accents (`é`
to `e`, `ß` to `ss`). Anything else separates words.

```csharp
Text.Slugify("Lahore Fort, 2024"); // "lahore-fort-2024"
Text.Slugify("لاہور قلعہ"); // "لاہور-قلعہ"
Text.Slugify("لاہور Fort", new SlugifyOptions { Script = SlugScript.Latin }); // "fort"
Text.Slugify("کراچی ۲۰۲۴", new SlugifyOptions { Script = SlugScript.Urdu }); // "کراچی-2024"
```

params.name: input
params.doc: Text to turn into a slug.

params.name: options
params.doc: Which letters to keep; `null` keeps Latin and Urdu.

returns.doc: The slug, or `""` when nothing is left (or the input is `null`). Never throws.

methods.name: CompareUrdu
methods.signature: public static int CompareUrdu(string? a, string? b)
methods.doc:
Compares two strings in Urdu alphabetical order, for sorting
(`list.Sort(Text.CompareUrdu)`).

Letters follow the Unicode CLDR collation for Urdu (`ur`, CLDR 49):
ا آ ب بھ پ پھ ت تھ ٹ ٹھ ث ج جھ چ چھ ح خ د دھ ڈ ڈھ ذ ر رھ ڑ ڑھ ز ژ س ش ص ض
ط ظ ع غ ف ق ک کھ گ گھ ل لھ م مھ ن نھ ں ںھ و وھ ہ ھ ۃ ء ی یھ ے. A letter
joined with ھ is a letter of its own (so بھ comes after every other ب
word). أ ؤ ۂ ئ ۓ sort as ا و ہ ی ے and come just after them when words
are otherwise equal, and diacritics only break ties, in CLDR's order.

Outside the Urdu letters: spaces and punctuation come first, then
digits digit by digit (Urdu, Arabic-Indic and ASCII digits are equal;
`10` comes before `2`), then Urdu letters, then other
Arabic-script characters (the look-alikes ك ي ى ه ة, which CLDR does
not treat as Urdu letters), then everything else by code point,
ignoring ASCII case. Strings that are still equal are ordered by code
point, so the result is 0 only for identical strings. The order is
built in, so it does not depend on the machine's culture or ICU.

```csharp
var words = new List<string> { "ے", "بھائی", "آم", "باغ", "اب" };
words.Sort(Text.CompareUrdu); // اب, آم, باغ, بھائی, ے
```

returns.doc: `-1`, `0` or `1`. Never throws.

methods.name: IsRtl
methods.doc:
Whether text reads right to left: its first letter is from a
right-to-left script such as Urdu or Arabic. Digits, punctuation and
spaces are skipped, as in the Unicode bidirectional algorithm's
paragraph rule.

```csharp
Text.IsRtl("سلام"); // true
Text.IsRtl("123 سلام"); // true
Text.IsRtl("Order نمبر"); // false
```

returns.doc: `false` when there is no letter, or the input is `null`. Never throws.

methods.name: WrapBidi
methods.signature: public static string WrapBidi(string? text, BidiDirection direction = BidiDirection.Auto)
methods.doc:
Wraps text in Unicode directional isolates, so a name or number in one
direction does not reorder the sentence around it (for example an
English order number inside an Urdu message).

Uses FIRST STRONG ISOLATE (U+2068) for {@link BidiDirection.Auto},
RIGHT-TO-LEFT ISOLATE (U+2067) for {@link BidiDirection.Rtl} and
LEFT-TO-RIGHT ISOLATE (U+2066) for {@link BidiDirection.Ltr},
closed with POP DIRECTIONAL ISOLATE (U+2069). Any other value counts as
{@link BidiDirection.Auto}.

```csharp
$"آرڈر {Text.WrapBidi("PDK-1042")} بھیج دیا گیا";
```

returns.doc: The wrapped text, or `""` when the input is `null`. Never throws.

methods.name: Calculate
methods.doc:
Income tax to withhold or collect under one section of the Income Tax
Ordinance 2001, for a person on or not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List,
from FBR's Withholding Tax Rate Card for tax years 2025 to 2027.

Covered: 231AB cash withdrawal, 236C sale and 236K purchase of
immovable property, 151 profit on debt, 150 dividends, 153 goods,
services and contracts, 154B social media income (from 2027) and 149
salary (the salaried rate table, as {@link IncomeTax.CalculateSalaryTax}).

The rate for a person not on the list follows each case's own rule in
the Tenth Schedule: usually double, but a fixed rate (236C, and 151 in
2025), its own value bands (236K), or none (149; 231AB applies only to
them). The rate applies to the whole amount (236C and 236K value bands
are not marginal), and the tax is rounded to the nearest rupee (section
219). Where FBR's card and the Ordinance differ, the Ordinance is used
and {@link WithholdingTax.StatuteOverride} says so.

For 231AB, pass the day's total of all cash withdrawals: nothing is
collected up to Rs 50,000. For 150 mutual fund dividends received by a
company, the debt part is `mutual-fund-debt-part-company` (29%).
For 151 sukuk held by an individual or AOP, the case must fit the
return on investment ({@link WithholdingInput.ReturnOnInvestment}),
and exactly Rs 1 million gives `null`. For 154B, give
{@link WithholdingInput.Resident} to get
{@link WithholdingTax.TaxNature}.

This is an estimate from the rate card, not tax advice: exemptions,
reduced-rate certificates, adjustable or final status and the many
cases not listed here are not applied.

```csharp
Withholding.Calculate(new WithholdingInput { Section = "236K", Amount = 60_000_000, Atl = false, TaxYear = 2027 });
// Rate = 14.5, Tax = 8700000, NonAtlRule = Slabs, …
```

entries.doc:
Zakat deducted at source in Pakistan: the nisab notified each year by the
Administrator-General Zakat and conveyed to banks by SBP (Zakat years 1433
to 1447 AH, 2012-2026), and the deduction from one account.

This is the nisab for deduction from savings and similar bank accounts
under the Zakat and Ushr Ordinance 1980, not a religious ruling on
personal Zakat.

methods.name: GetNisab
methods.doc:
The nisab for compulsory Zakat deduction at source for a Zakat year,
given by its Hijri year or a date in it.

A Zakat year starts on 1 Ramazan ({@link ZakatNisab.Ramazan1}, as
the Central Ruet-e-Hilal Committee announced it), and a date belongs to
the last year whose 1 Ramazan is on or before it. A date before the
first covered year, or 353 days or more after the last year's 1 Ramazan
(the next year not yet notified), gives `null`.

```csharp
Zakat.GetNisab(new ZakatYearQuery { ZakatYear = 1447 })?.Nisab;    // 503529
Zakat.GetNisab(new ZakatYearQuery { Label = "1445-46" })?.ZakatYear; // 1446
Zakat.GetNisab(new ZakatYearQuery { Date = "2025-06-01" })?.Nisab;  // 179689
```

returns.doc: The year's nisab, dates and sources, or `null` for a year that is not covered or an invalid query. Never throws.

methods.doc:
The nisab for compulsory Zakat deduction at source for a Hijri Zakat year.

```csharp

```

methods.name: CalculateDeduction
methods.signature:
public static ZakatDeduction? CalculateDeduction(
    double balance,
    ZakatYearQuery? query,
    bool exempt = false)
methods.doc:
Zakat deducted at source from one account on the valuation date (1
Ramazan): 2.5% of the whole balance, rounded to the nearest rupee
(First Schedule, Note 2), when it is at or above that year's nisab, and
nothing when it is below or the holder has a valid exemption
declaration (Form CZ-50).

A balance exactly equal to the nisab is deducted: every notification
says no deduction where the balance is "less than" the nisab, and the
Ordinance (s. 2(xxiii)) defines a sahib-e-nisab as owning "not less
than nisab". The First Schedule's own wording ("does not exceed") would
not deduct it. In Punjab the Punjab Zakat and Ushr Act 2018 replaced
the Ordinance, with the same First Schedule wording.

It applies to the accounts the Ordinance subjects to deduction at
source: savings, profit-and-loss sharing and similar accounts (asset
code 101). Current accounts and foreign currency accounts are not
deducted. It is not a religious ruling on how much Zakat a person owes.

```csharp
Zakat.CalculateDeduction(600_000, new ZakatYearQuery { ZakatYear = 1447 });
// ZakatYear = 1447, Nisab = 503529, Balance = 600000, Deductible = true,
// Reason = null, Rate = 2.5, Zakat = 15000, Source = { … }
Zakat.CalculateDeduction(600_000, new ZakatYearQuery { ZakatYear = 1447 }, exempt: true)?.Zakat; // 0
```

params.name: balance
params.doc: The account balance in rupees at the start of the valuation date, 0 to 1 trillion.

params.name: query
params.doc: The Zakat year or a date in it.

params.name: exempt
params.doc: `true` if the holder has a valid exemption declaration (Form CZ-50) with the bank: filed at least 30 days before the valuation date, sworn before a magistrate, oath commissioner, notary public or other person authorised to administer oaths, in the presence of two witnesses (Zakat and Ushr Ordinance 1980, s. 1(3), proviso (a)). The library does not check the declaration.

returns.doc: The deduction and its source, or `null` for an invalid balance or a year that is not covered. Never throws.
